Subject Name: 未来エネルギー創成[Future Energy Creation]
Theme: Course Orientation / Fundamentals of Thermodynamics / Types of Energy and Physical Constants
Details: This lecture explains the overall purpose of the course, demonstrating why thermodynamics is crucial for considering energy production. It organizes fundamental concepts such as energy, work, and heat, providing a scientific understanding of representative energy forms, including kinetic energy, potential energy, chemical energy, electrical energy, and thermal energy. It confirms the meaning of units and physical constants frequently used in thermodynamics, solidifying the foundation for understanding future lectures.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 未来エネルギー創成[Future Energy Creation]
Details: We examine the First Law of Thermodynamics, known as the law of energy conservation, and learn about the relationship between internal energy, heat, and work. Through the process of energy changing form, moving, and transforming, we understand the concept of energy balance. Using concrete examples such as power generation and chemical reactions, we consider why, despite energy never being lost, there are constraints on how it can be utilized.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 未来エネルギー創成[Future Energy Creation]
Details: This section addresses the Second Law of Thermodynamics, which governs the irreversibility of natural phenomena. It introduces the concept of entropy and provides a scientific explanation for why energy conversion inevitably involves loss and why not all energy can be effectively utilized. Using the upper limit of thermal engine efficiency as an example, it helps understand that fundamental limitations exist in energy utilization.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 未来エネルギー創成[Future Energy Creation]
Details: Introduce the concept of free energy and learn which portion of energy can be extracted as work. Focusing on Gibbs free energy, understand the relationship with reactions that proceed spontaneously and with equilibrium states. Through these concepts, be able to thermodynamically explain why chemical reactions and battery reactions proceed.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 未来エネルギー創成[Future Energy Creation]
Details: We examine exergy as an indicator that evaluates not only the “quantity” but also the “quality” of energy. By considering the First and Second Laws of Thermodynamics, we learn to compare electrical energy with high-temperature heat and low-temperature heat, and to evaluate energy from the perspective of usability. This enables a scientific understanding of why waste heat and untapped energy resources arise.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 未来エネルギー創成[Future Energy Creation]
Details: Batteries are examined as representative energy conversion and storage devices, explaining the relationship between chemical energy and electrical energy from a thermodynamic perspective. Students will understand the relationship between a battery's electromotive force and free energy change, learning the physical significance of metrics such as energy density and efficiency. Through examples like lithium-ion batteries and fuel cells, the fundamentals of energy conversion technology will be understood.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 未来エネルギー創成[Future Energy Creation]
Details: Using the thermodynamic concepts learned thus far, examine energy issues in renewable energy and a decarbonized society. Considering the thermodynamic constraints associated with energy conversion and storage, develop the perspective to scientifically evaluate entire energy systems while distinguishing between what is technically feasible and what presents difficulties.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 未来エネルギー創成[Future Energy Creation]
Details: We will review the fundamental concepts of thermodynamics covered throughout the course and their applications, reaffirming the perspective for scientifically explaining energy generation. Subsequently, a final exam will be administered to assess conceptual understanding and logical explanatory skills.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Theme: What is Policy Sociology: Sociology and Public Policy
Details: Burawoy's four types, positioning of policy sociology, relationship between sociology and public policy. Work: Identify familiar policies and consider who designed them with what assumptions.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅠ[Contemporary Sociology D1]
Theme: Understanding Public Policy: Policy Process and Actors
Details: Policy cycle (problem definition → agenda setting → formation → decision → implementation → evaluation), foundations of policy process theory, actor mapping. Work: Map policy actors for child/childcare support.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅠ[Contemporary Sociology D1]
Theme: State, Governance, and Institutions: Who Decides Policy
Details: Political sociology and state theory, welfare state theory (Esping-Andersen, etc.), governance theory. Work: Compare "state-centered model" and "governance network model" in healthcare/elderly care.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅠ[Contemporary Sociology D1]
Theme: Evidence, Expert Knowledge and Policy: Sociology of EBPM
Details: EBPM ideals and reality, role and limitations of social surveys/statistics, epistemic communities. Work: Examine "what is measured and what is invisible" in white papers/statistics.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅠ[Contemporary Sociology D1]
Theme: Inequality and Social Policy: Class, Gender, and Minorities
Details: Class/poverty/precarity and social policy, gender order and family policy, minority policy and inclusion/exclusion. Work: Extract family models/labor views underlying welfare/parental leave policies.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅠ[Contemporary Sociology D1]
Theme: Risk, Environment, and Globalization: Policy from Contemporary Social Theory
Details: Risk society theory/environmental sociology, globalization and policy (international organizations/multinationals/citizen movements), Japanese issues (aging/regional revitalization). Work: Critical examination of SDGs targets and Japanese policies.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅠ[Contemporary Sociology D1]
Theme: Possibilities and Limitations of Policy Sociology: Summary and Group Presentations
Details: Review of key concepts, self-reflection on policy sociology (dilemma between client orientation and criticality). Group presentations: Each group analyzes one policy topic sociologically (approx. 10 min).

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅡ[Contemporary Sociology D2]
Details: Aims and procedures of policy sociology research. Introduction to typical research themes. Group formation and theme selection. Homework: Find 2 policy documents and 1 academic paper.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅡ[Contemporary Sociology D2]
Theme: Finding Literature/Resources and Prior Research Review
Details: Types and roles of literature (academic papers, policy documents, statistical data). Basics of literature review. Group literature introduction and organization. Homework: Create 2-3 page literature review.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅡ[Contemporary Sociology D2]
Theme: Creating Analytical Framework: How to Use Theory
Details: Introduction to representative analytical axes (inequality, governance, risk, evidence). Create concept maps in groups. How to apply theory to own cases. Homework: Write 1-2 page analytical framework.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅡ[Contemporary Sociology D2]
Theme: Reading Policy Documents and Data: Case Study Design
Details: How to read policy documents (problem definition, goals, institutional design, etc.). How to select cases (time series, regional comparison, etc.). Group policy document analysis. Interim report. Homework: Create 3-4 page interim report.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅡ[Contemporary Sociology D2]
Details: Policy evaluation perspectives (distributional impact, normative aspects, implementation gaps). Discussion of current policy issues and improvement directions. Alternative proposal conception. Homework: Create draft slides/handouts for final presentation.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅡ[Contemporary Sociology D2]
Theme: Final Presentation Preparation and Peer Review
Details: Presentation structure (problem setting → prior research → framework → analysis → implications). Practice presentations by groups. Feedback using peer review sheets. Homework: Complete final presentation materials.

Subject Name: 現代社会学ＤⅡ[Contemporary Sociology D2]
Details: Each group presents 10-12 min + 5 min Q&A. Instructor comments (theoretical contributions, future development potential). Overall discussion: Strengths and limitations of policy sociological approaches. Submit individual final report.

政策社会学[Policy Sociology]
Theme: What is Policy Sociology: Sociology and Public Policy
Details: Burawoy's four types, positioning of policy sociology, relationship between sociology and public policy. Work: Identify familiar policies and consider who designed them with what assumptions.

Subject Name: 政策社会学[Policy Sociology]
Theme: Understanding Public Policy: Policy Process and Actors
Details: Policy cycle (problem definition → agenda setting → formation → decision → implementation → evaluation), foundations of policy process theory, actor mapping. Work: Map policy actors for child/childcare support.

Subject Name: 政策社会学[Policy Sociology]
Theme: State, Governance, and Institutions: Who Decides Policy
Details: Political sociology and state theory, welfare state theory (Esping-Andersen, etc.), governance theory. Work: Compare "state-centered model" and "governance network model" in healthcare/elderly care.

Subject Name: 政策社会学[Policy Sociology]
Theme: Evidence, Expert Knowledge and Policy: Sociology of EBPM
Details: EBPM ideals and reality, role and limitations of social surveys/statistics, epistemic communities. Work: Examine "what is measured and what is invisible" in white papers/statistics.

Subject Name: 政策社会学[Policy Sociology]
Theme: Inequality and Social Policy: Class, Gender, and Minorities
Details: Class/poverty/precarity and social policy, gender order and family policy, minority policy and inclusion/exclusion. Work: Extract family models/labor views underlying welfare/parental leave policies.

Subject Name: 政策社会学[Policy Sociology]
Theme: Risk, Environment, and Globalization: Policy from Contemporary Social Theory
Details: Risk society theory/environmental sociology, globalization and policy (international organizations/multinationals/citizen movements), Japanese issues (aging/regional revitalization). Work: Critical examination of SDGs targets and Japanese policies.

Subject Name: 政策社会学[Policy Sociology]
Theme: Possibilities and Limitations of Policy Sociology: Summary and Group Presentations
Details: Review of key concepts, self-reflection on policy sociology (dilemma between client orientation and criticality). Group presentations: Each group analyzes one policy topic sociologically (approx. 10 min).

Subject Name: 政策社会学研究[Studies on Policy Sociology]
Details: Aims and procedures of policy sociology research. Introduction to typical research themes. Group formation and theme selection. Homework: Find 2 policy documents and 1 academic paper.

Subject Name: 政策社会学研究[Studies on Policy Sociology]
Theme: Finding Literature/Resources and Prior Research Review
Details: Types and roles of literature (academic papers, policy documents, statistical data). Basics of literature review. Group literature introduction and organization. Homework: Create 2-3 page literature review.

Subject Name: 政策社会学研究[Studies on Policy Sociology]
Theme: Creating Analytical Framework: How to Use Theory
Details: Introduction to representative analytical axes (inequality, governance, risk, evidence). Create concept maps in groups. How to apply theory to own cases. Homework: Write 1-2 page analytical framework.

Subject Name: 政策社会学研究[Studies on Policy Sociology]
Theme: Reading Policy Documents and Data: Case Study Design
Details: How to read policy documents (problem definition, goals, institutional design, etc.). How to select cases (time series, regional comparison, etc.). Group policy document analysis. Interim report. Homework: Create 3-4 page interim report.

Subject Name: 政策社会学研究[Studies on Policy Sociology]
Details: Policy evaluation perspectives (distributional impact, normative aspects, implementation gaps). Discussion of current policy issues and improvement directions. Alternative proposal conception. Homework: Create draft slides/handouts for final presentation.

Subject Name: 政策社会学研究[Studies on Policy Sociology]
Theme: Final Presentation Preparation and Peer Review
Details: Presentation structure (problem setting → prior research → framework → analysis → implications). Practice presentations by groups. Feedback using peer review sheets. Homework: Complete final presentation materials.

Subject Name: 政策社会学研究[Studies on Policy Sociology]
Details: Each group presents 10-12 min + 5 min Q&A. Instructor comments (theoretical contributions, future development potential). Overall discussion: Strengths and limitations of policy sociological approaches. Submit individual final report.

心理学研究法２Ａ[Psychological Research Methods 2A]
Details: Students overview the general linear model, which forms the foundation of statistical modeling. In the practical session, they experience conducting an online survey using Google Forms, followed by learning how to use R and R Studio.

Subject Name: 心理学研究法２Ａ[Psychological Research Methods 2A]
Details: Students learn the meaning of t-values and p-values through simulations of the t-test and become able to explain Type I and Type II errors. In the practical session, they master how to plot the t-distribution.

Subject Name: 心理学研究法２Ａ[Psychological Research Methods 2A]
Theme: Effects size and sample size design
Details: Students learn about the relationship between test statistics and effect size. In the practical session, they calculate the sample size required for determining experimental designs.

Subject Name: 心理学研究法２Ａ[Psychological Research Methods 2A]
Details: Students learn about simple linear regression analysis, which consists of two variables: an independent variable and a dependent variable. In the practical session, they learn how to draw scatter plots and regression lines.

Subject Name: 心理学研究法２Ａ[Psychological Research Methods 2A]
Details: Students learn about regression analysis for non-continuous variables.  In the practical session, create simulation data and practice generating summary tables and graphs.

Subject Name: 心理学研究法２Ａ[Psychological Research Methods 2A]
Details: Students learn methods to remove the confounding effect between two independent variables in order to establish a foundation in multiple linear regression analysis. In the practical session, they create simulated data that has a correlation between the two variables.

Subject Name: 心理学研究法２Ａ[Psychological Research Methods 2A]
Details: Students learn about multiple regression analysis which is a regression model with multiple independent variables. In the practical session, they address the issue of multicollinearity using simulation data.

Subject Name: 心理学研究法２Ａ[Psychological Research Methods 2A]
Details: When analyzing experimental data, several situations may arise where judgment is required regarding normality, homogeneity of variance, and statistical power. Students verify what issues may arise in these scenarios through data generation.

Subject Name: 心理学研究法２Ｂ[Psychological Research Methods 2B]
Details: Students learn about path analysis, which describes the relationships between variables. In the practical session, they practice constructing simple and multiple regression models and mediation analysis.

Subject Name: 心理学研究法２Ｂ[Psychological Research Methods 2B]
Details: Students learn about factor analysis models that handle latent variables. In the practical session, they perform confirmatory factor analysis using simulation data.

Subject Name: 心理学研究法２Ｂ[Psychological Research Methods 2B]
Details: Students learn about parameter estimation methods for factor analysis. In the practical session, they perform exploratory factor analysis using simulation data.

Subject Name: 心理学研究法２Ｂ[Psychological Research Methods 2B]
Details: Students learn about principal component analysis (PCA) which is used to summarize multivariable data. In the practical session, they confirm the differences with factor analysis.

Subject Name: 心理学研究法２Ｂ[Psychological Research Methods 2B]
Details: Students learn about models incorporating random effects. In the practical session, they solve an ANOVA including within-subjects factors using a linear mixed model.

Subject Name: 心理学研究法２Ｂ[Psychological Research Methods 2B]
Details: Students learn about generalized linear model as a modeling approach when the dependent variable does not follow a normal distribution. In the practical session, they generate and analyze data with assumed upper and lower bounds, as well as probabilistic data.

Subject Name: 心理学研究法２Ｂ[Psychological Research Methods 2B]
Details: Students learn structural equation modeling (covariance structure analysis) which incorporates all the techniques introduced up to this section. In the practical exercises, they practice drawing the relationships between equations including latent variables as path diagrams.

Subject Name: 心理学研究法２Ｂ[Psychological Research Methods 2B]
Details: Students perform analysis of data collected through experiments or surveys, or simulation data using statistical methods learned through these classes. They resolve any questions regarding the statistical methods they have performed.

地球惑星物理学Ａ[Earth and Planetary Physics A]
Theme: The shape of the Earth and moment of inertia
Details: This course aims to understand the shape of a planet in terms of gravity, centrifugal force, flattening, density structure, and moment of inertia.

Subject Name: 地球惑星物理学Ａ[Earth and Planetary Physics A]
Details: This course aims to understand that the gravity potential describes the shape of the Earth, to understand the meaning of the equation of the gravity potential, and to understand the relationship between the flattening (f) and J2.

Subject Name: 地球惑星物理学Ａ[Earth and Planetary Physics A]
Theme: Geoid, geoid anomaly, gravity anomaly (free-air anomaly, Bouguer anomaly)
Details: This course aims to understand geoid, geoid anomaly, and gravity anomaly, to understand relations between geoid anomaly/gravity anomaly and the structure of the Earth’s interior, and to calculate a gravity anomaly.

Subject Name: 地球惑星物理学Ａ[Earth and Planetary Physics A]
Details: This course aims to understand stress and strain, to understand elastic modulus (Young’s modulus, bulk modulus, rigidity, Poisson’s ratio), and to be able to calculate stress, strain, and elastic moduli.

Subject Name: 地球惑星物理学Ａ[Earth and Planetary Physics A]
Details: This course aims to understand what a stress tensor is, to understand the relation between a stress tensor and a traction, to understand lithostatic equilibrium and isostacy.

Subject Name: 地球惑星物理学Ａ[Earth and Planetary Physics A]
Details: This course aims to understand displacement vector and strain tensor, to understand that the sum of the diagonal components of the strain tensor is equal to the area strain (two-dimensional) or the volume strain (three-dimensional), to understand the deformation described by a strain tensor, and to understand the principal stress/strain, the principal stress/strain axis, and the rotation of a tensor.

Subject Name: 地球惑星物理学Ａ[Earth and Planetary Physics A]
Details: This course aims to understand Lamé’s constants, to understand the relationship between elastic constants and stress/strain in isotropic body, to understand the four elastic constants in isotropic elastic-body and the relationship between seismic velocities and Lamé's constants, and to understand the condition of the balance of stress in an infinitesimal element.

Subject Name: 地球惑星物理学Ａ[Earth and Planetary Physics A]
Details: We take the exam and review the content of this lecture.

Subject Name: 地球惑星物理学Ｂ[Earth and Planetary Physics B]
Theme: Propagation of seismic waves: equation of motion in elastic body
Details: This course aims to understand that the equation of motion in elastic body gives two types of wave equations, to understand that the two wave equations correspond to the wave equations of P and S waves, to find the general solution (d'Alembert's solution) to the one-dimensional wave equation and understand its meaning, to solve one-dimensional wave equation under given conditions.

Subject Name: 地球惑星物理学Ｂ[Earth and Planetary Physics B]
Theme: Seismic waves: P and S waves, surface waves, Earth’s free oscillation & Snell's law
Details: This course aims to understand seismic waves (P, S, and surface waves, Earth’s free oscillation), to understand the relationship between the propagation direction and the oscillation direction for plain P and S waves, and to understand the Snell's law.

Subject Name: 地球惑星物理学Ｂ[Earth and Planetary Physics B]
Theme: Travel time curve and the structure of the Earth (I)
Details: This course aims to understand the structure of the Earth’s interior estimated from travel time curve, to understand the velocity distribution of P and S waves of the Earth’s interior, and to understand a cause of the velocity discontinuity of the Earth’s interior.

Subject Name: 地球惑星物理学Ｂ[Earth and Planetary Physics B]
Theme: The structure of the Earth (II) & Clapeyron slope
Details: This course aims to understand the distribution of density, pressure, bulk modulus, rigidity, gravity, and temperature in the Earth's interior, to understand the Adams-Williamson's equation, to understand images of seismic tomography, to understand the relationship among Clapeyron slope, phase transition, and mantle convection.

Subject Name: 地球惑星物理学Ｂ[Earth and Planetary Physics B]
Details: This course aims to understand the magnitude of an earthquake, to understand seismic moment, to understand scaling laws of earthquakes, to understand active faults.

Subject Name: 地球惑星物理学Ｂ[Earth and Planetary Physics B]
Theme: Fault movement and mechanism of earthquake
Details: This course aims to understand the relationship between stress field and fault movement, to understand the relationship between fault movement and the double couple model, and to understand the relationship between plate boundary, hypocenter distribution, and focal mechanism.

Subject Name: 地球惑星物理学Ｂ[Earth and Planetary Physics B]
Theme: Diversity of fault movement and frictional constitutive law
Details: This course aims to understand a relationship between fault movement, radiated seismic waves, and asperity, to understand a spatial relationship between asperity, hypocenter and aftershocks, to understand slow earthquakes, to understand a diversity of fault movement based on a frictional constitutive law.

Subject Name: 地球惑星物理学Ｂ[Earth and Planetary Physics B]

ゲノム科学Ａ[Genome Science A]
Theme: Life Information: Why is DNA Necessary?
Details: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) serves as the fundamental molecule for storing and transmitting genetic information in all living organisms. Its stability, ability to replicate accurately, and capacity to encode complex biological instructions make it essential for life. DNA sequences determine the structure and function of proteins, which in turn regulate cellular processes and organismal development.
Instructor: 堀家　慎一 | [ | HORIKE, Shin-ichi | ](疾患モデル総合研究センター 研究基盤支援施設)

Subject Name: ゲノム科学Ａ[Genome Science A]
Details: A gene is a functional unit of genetic information encoded within DNA. It contains sequences that guide the synthesis of RNA and proteins, which perform essential cellular functions. Genes include coding regions (exons) that determine protein sequences and regulatory regions that control gene expression.
Instructor: 堀家　慎一 | [ | HORIKE, Shin-ichi | ](疾患モデル総合研究センター 研究基盤支援施設)

Subject Name: ゲノム科学Ａ[Genome Science A]
Details: The genome refers to the complete set of genetic material within an organism. In eukaryotes, genomic DNA is stored in the nucleus as linear chromosomes, while in prokaryotes, it exists as a circular molecule in the cytoplasm. The genome contains both protein-coding genes and vast non-coding regions that contribute to gene regulation and genome organization.

Theme: Chromatin and the Epigenome: Additional Information on the Genome
Details: Chromatin is the complex of DNA and proteins (mainly histones) that compacts and organizes genomic DNA within the nucleus. The epigenome refers to chemical modifications to DNA and histones, such as DNA methylation and histone modifications, which influence gene expression without altering the DNA sequence itself. These modifications play a crucial role in development, cellular differentiation, and response to environmental factors.

教師論[Theories on Teacher Education]
Theme: Orientation: Teacher Qualities Considered Through a Comedy Sketch
Details: Organize and think about the reasons why you want to obtain a teaching license. | Get an idea of ​​the future of ICT education and learn how to use basic apps used in class.

Subject Name: 教師論[Theories on Teacher Education]
Details: Learn about the differences between perspectives, viewpoints, and viewpoints in the teaching profession. | In order to become an attractive teacher to students, consider the qualities of a teacher using romantic issues as a topic. | This content is also useful for university students about to embark on their university life.

Subject Name: 教師論[Theories on Teacher Education]
Theme: Chapter 2: History of Japan's Education System and Teacher Training 1: From Ancient Times to the Early Modern Period | "Learning to read and write is like acquiring a time machine"
Details: Who is education for? Nowadays, it is for the entire nation, but in the past, it was a tool for those in power, such as kings, nobles, and samurai. Learning history is not about memorizing, but about acquiring important items that will help us know the future. Those who do not learn history will end up repeating the same mistakes.

Subject Name: 教師論[Theories on Teacher Education]
Theme: Chapter 2: History of Japan's Education System and Teacher Training 2: Education from the Taisho Era to the Present | "What kind of education prevents us from participating in war?"
Details: Demon Slayer is set in the Taisho era. As citizens gained power, various liberal education methods were proposed. However, militaristic education led teachers to become complicit in the war. | Learning about this process will lead to education that will prevent children from being sent to the battlefield again.

Subject Name: 教師論[Theories on Teacher Education]
Details: Public school teachers are bound by the "Special Act on Educational Public Servants," which is even stricter than local government employees. We will consider the content and reasons for this law, as well as the meaning of the law protecting teachers who provide education.

Subject Name: 教師論[Theories on Teacher Education]
Theme: Today's Educational Issues 1: International Education, SDGs | Special Lecture: House of Joy Children's Home, Education in the Philippines.
Details: We will invite Mr. Sawamura, who runs a children's home in the Philippines, to talk about running the home and what he values. We will look at how to treat children who are separated from their parents and Mr. Sawamura's life abroad (the timing will depend on the other party's schedule, so this will be held at one of the 15 sessions).

Subject Name: 教師論[Theories on Teacher Education]
Theme: Chapter 4: Mental Health of Teachers | How to Build Resilience
Details: Analyze the current situation where there are said to be few people wanting to become teachers, consider the factors and countermeasures, and consider ways to help teachers develop a resilient spirit.

Subject Name: 教師論[Theories on Teacher Education]
Theme: Chapter 5: Improving Teacher Qualification and Training | The qualities and abilities required for teachers - what remains the same and what changes
Details: There are some qualities and abilities that teachers need to have that don't change and some that need to change. | I'd like to hear your opinions on these two abilities. | Understand the content of the legal training that will be given to teachers after they become teachers

Subject Name: 教師論[Theories on Teacher Education]

Details: We all make mistakes. So, is it impossible to prevent medical accidents? If we view accidents as individual problems such as distraction and personality problems, we will not reach a fundamental solution. It is necessary to understand the points at which people make mistakes and take countermeasures in the system.

Subject Name: 臨床医学の共通基盤[Clinical Foundation]
Theme: Incident Reporting and Care Process Improvement.
Details: What is “incident reporting”? It is often thought of as an apology or a remorse report, but it is not. Behind every incident is a hidden structural problem. If structural problems are not resolved, the same incidents will occur again, even if the individual is blamed and encouraged to reflect on the problem. Incident reports should be viewed as a business improvement plan that point out structural problems and encourages improvement.

Theme: The Emergence of Minamata Disease and the Division of the Local Community: Why Was Environmental Pollution Not Stopped?
Details: This class explores why Minamata disease occurred and why it continued for many years. It examines not only the health damage caused by pollution, but also how the disaster divided the local community. The class also analyzes the structural features behind the Minamata case and treats it as a present-day issue rather than something that belongs only to the past. We will discuss how similar structural problems can emerge in contemporary society and consider ways to prevent such tragedies from occurring again, examining the issue from the perspectives of the national government, corporations, local governments, and citizens. | Before the class, research the Minamata disease case and identify at least two factors that allowed the damage to continue for many years. Details: A video material about an NGO engaged in environmental conservation and human rights protection in Riau Province, Indonesia is presented. After watching it, students will exchange opinions on the social significance of NGO organizations and write a report.
Instructor: 小髙　敬寛 | [ | ODAKA, Takahiro | ](国際基幹教育院 GS教育系)

Subject Name: KUGS実践[Multicultural Co-creative Learning for KUGS]

Details: A follow-up video of the one presented in the previous week, which explores the causes and current situation of environmental issues in Riau Province in depth, will be presented. After watching it, students will exchange opinions on what we should do in response to globalizing environmental problems and then write a report.
Instructor: 小髙　敬寛 | [ | ODAKA, Takahiro | ](国際基幹教育院 GS教育系)

Subject Name: KUGS実践[Multicultural Co-creative Learning for KUGS]
Details: In this lecture, students will survey the trends and characteristics of foreign migration into Ishikawa Prefecture, and examine the activities of various actors involved in accepting foreign workers. Through discussions and related activities, students will also reflect on the meaning of coexistence.
Instructor: 眞住　優助 | [ | MAZUMI, Yusuke | ](国際基幹教育院 GS教育系)

Subject Name: KUGS実践[Multicultural Co-creative Learning for KUGS]

Subject Name: KUGS実践[Multicultural Co-creative Learning for KUGS]
Theme: The Emergence of Minamata Disease and the Division of the Local Community: Why Was Environmental Pollution Not Stopped?
Details: This class explores why Minamata disease occurred and why it continued for many years. It examines not only the health damage caused by pollution, but also how the disaster divided the local community. The class also analyzes the structural features behind the Minamata case and treats it as a present-day issue rather than something that belongs only to the past. We will discuss how similar structural problems can emerge in contemporary society and consider ways to prevent such tragedies from occurring again, examining the issue from the perspectives of the national government, corporations, local governments, and citizens. | Before the class, research the Minamata disease case and identify at least two factors that allowed the damage to continue for many years. In 150 words or more, explain your reasoning. | After the first class, submit a written response of  150 words or more addressing the following topic: Propose an institutional design to overcome the “Minamata-type structure.”
Instructor: 飯田　玲子 | [ | IIDA, Reiko | ](国際基幹教育院 GS教育系)

We will clarify the meaning of quantum numbers and the concept of electron configuration, solidifying the foundation for understanding the properties of matter at the atomic level.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 化学ⅡＡ[Fundamental Chemistry 2A]
Theme: Review: Periodic Table, Properties of Atoms and Elements
Details: Review the development of the periodic table and periodicity, and learn how atomic properties such as atomic radius and electronegativity change. Acquire the ability to predict element properties using the periodic table.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 化学ⅡＡ[Fundamental Chemistry 2A]
Theme: Review: Chemical Bonds and Molecular Structure
Details: Review the fundamental concepts of chemical bonds, such as covalent and ionic bonds, and learn about their relationship to molecular shape and structure. Understand how molecular structure influences the properties and reactivity of substances.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 化学ⅡＡ[Fundamental Chemistry 2A]
Details: Learn fundamental thermodynamic concepts such as energy, work, and heat. Understand the basics for viewing chemical reactions from an energy perspective and aim to become familiar with thermodynamic thinking.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 化学ⅡＡ[Fundamental Chemistry 2A]
Details: Learn about energy changes accompanying chemical reactions and understand the difference between exothermic and endothermic reactions. The goal is to be able to qualitatively explain why reactions occur from an energy perspective.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 化学ⅡＡ[Fundamental Chemistry 2A]
Details: Learn the concept of chemical equilibrium and understand the conditions under which reactions proceed or cease. Organize the reasons why equilibrium states occur and develop the ability to analyze chemical reactions using the concept of equilibrium.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 化学ⅡＡ[Fundamental Chemistry 2A]
Details: Learn the basic definitions and properties of acids and bases. Understand how acids and bases are involved in chemical reactions and everyday phenomena through neutralization reactions and familiar examples.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 化学ⅡＡ[Fundamental Chemistry 2A]
Details: Comprehensively review the material covered thus far and consolidate your understanding of fundamental chemical concepts. Through the final exam, assess your ability to logically explain phenomena ranging from atomic and molecular levels to chemical reactions.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 化学ⅡＢ[Fundamental Chemistry 2B]
Details: Focusing on the speed at which chemical reactions proceed, we learn the fundamental concepts of reaction rate. Through the energy barrier and the influence of temperature, we understand the conditions under which reactions occur.

Subject Name: 化学ⅡＢ[Fundamental Chemistry 2B]
Details: As a foundation of organic chemistry, we examine hydrocarbons and learn about the diversity of molecular structures. Through the concepts of stereochemistry, we understand how a molecule's shape influences its properties and reactivity.

Subject Name: 化学ⅡＢ[Fundamental Chemistry 2B]
Details: Learn about representative functional groups and understand the characteristics of their structures and properties. Organize the functions of organic molecules from the perspective of functional groups.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 化学ⅡＢ[Fundamental Chemistry 2B]
Details: Learn the fundamental structures of amino acids, peptides, and DNA as molecules that sustain life. Understand how chemical bonds and molecular structures are involved in biological phenomena.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Subject Name: 化学ⅡＢ[Fundamental Chemistry 2B]
Details: Comprehensively review the content learned in class to organize your understanding of chemical reactions, organic molecules, and biomolecules. Through the final exam, assess your ability to grasp chemistry in an interdisciplinary manner.
Instructor: 堀　優太 | [ | HORI, Yuta | ](融合研究域 融合科学系)

Details: The overall objectives, goals, schedule, and evaluation methods of the course will be explained. | Students will introduce themselves and share their academic backgrounds and areas of concern. | As the starting point of the course, students will attempt to relive and analyze the experience of "becoming a disaster victim" based on concrete case studies from past major disasters.

Subject Name: 防災・復興論[Disaster Mitigation and Recovery Studies]
Theme: Systems and Philosophies of Relief and Livelihood Recovery
Details: Students will learn about the processes and related systems from immediate post-disaster relief to long-term livelihood recovery, as well as the underlying philosophies that shape them.

Subject Name: 防災・復興論[Disaster Mitigation and Recovery Studies]
Theme: Urban Disasters and Reconstruction Case Studies
Details: This session focuses on case studies of urban disaster recovery, including reconstruction projects, urban planning, and community redevelopment processes following the Great Kanto Earthquake and the Great Hanshin-Awaji Earthquake.

Subject Name: 防災・復興論[Disaster Mitigation and Recovery Studies]
Theme: Recovery in Mountainous and Coastal Areas
Details: Students will study recovery processes in rural and coastal areas, including examples from the 2004 Niigata Chuetsu Earthquake, the 2007 Noto Peninsula Earthquake, and the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake. Topics include reconstruction projects, collective relocation, village restoration, and industrial recovery.

Subject Name: 防災・復興論[Disaster Mitigation and Recovery Studies]
Details: Based on case studies of the Great East Japan Earthquake and the 2019 Typhoon #19, students will explore how disaster information and community response influence evacuation in the face of floods and tsunamis.

Subject Name: 防災・復興論[Disaster Mitigation and Recovery Studies]
Details: Students will examine the role of volunteers in disaster recovery and risk reduction, how their roles differ from those of the public sector, and how related systems have evolved over time. | The concept of “support” itself will also be discussed, drawing insights from research in the field of care.

Subject Name: 防災・復興論[Disaster Mitigation and Recovery Studies]
Theme: Psychological Care and Disaster Memory Transmission
Details: This session introduces the basic concepts, institutional developments, and challenges of medicalization in psychological trauma care caused by disaster experiences. | Students will also study the transmission of disaster memory as part of the recovery process for victims and affected communities, focusing on case studies from the Hanshin-Awaji Earthquake and the Great East Japan Earthquake.

Subject Name: 防災・復興論[Disaster Mitigation and Recovery Studies]
Details: The course concludes with a written exam consisting of true/false questions to assess factual understanding and essay questions that address fundamental issues in disaster prevention and recovery.

Subject Name: 復興地域づくり論[Community-Based Post-Disaster Reconstruction]
Theme: What Is Reconstruction? — Concepts and Historical Cases
Details: This session introduces the concepts of restoration, reconstruction, and revitalization, and examines key features of reconstruction following the Hanshin-Awaji, Great East Japan, and Kumamoto earthquakes. Foundational policy documents such as the Basic Disaster Management Plan are also reviewed.
Instructor: 信岡　尚道[NOBUOKA, Hisamichi](能登里山里海未来創造センター)

Subject Name: 復興地域づくり論[Community-Based Post-Disaster Reconstruction]
Details: Students learn the institutional framework of large-scale disaster reconstruction, including the Reconstruction Act and special zone systems. Reconstruction plans from the Great East Japan and Kumamoto earthquakes are used to explore the relationship between reconstruction and urban planning.
Instructor: 信岡　尚道[NOBUOKA, Hisamichi](能登里山里海未来創造センター)

Subject Name: 復興地域づくり論[Community-Based Post-Disaster Reconstruction]
Theme: Restoration and Improved Restoration (From Emergency Repair to Seismic Reinforcement)
Details: This lecture covers emergency restoration and improved restoration of roads, bridges, and lifelines, including seismic reinforcement. Case studies from the Hanshin-Awaji, Niigata Chuetsu, and Kumamoto earthquakes illustrate practical approaches.
Instructor: 信岡　尚道[NOBUOKA, Hisamichi](能登里山里海未来創造センター)

Subject Name: 復興地域づくり論[Community-Based Post-Disaster Reconstruction]
Theme: Creative Reconstruction — Urban Restructuring and Regional Revitalization
Details: Students learn the principles of creative reconstruction and analyze urban revitalization cases such as Onagawa, Kesennuma, and Yuriage. The lecture examines spatial reconstruction measures including seawalls and land readjustment.
Instructor: 信岡　尚道[NOBUOKA, Hisamichi](能登里山里海未来創造センター)

Subject Name: 復興地域づくり論[Community-Based Post-Disaster Reconstruction]
Details: This session discusses the role of reconstruction councils and the challenges of consensus building, including issues of fairness and timeliness. Cases such as group relocation councils and citizen workshops are used to understand participatory reconstruction practices.
Instructor: 信岡　尚道[NOBUOKA, Hisamichi](能登里山里海未来創造センター)

Subject Name: 復興地域づくり論[Community-Based Post-Disaster Reconstruction]
Theme: Housing and Community Reconstruction and Urban Vitality
Details: Students study the transition from temporary to permanent housing and the challenges of rebuilding communities. Case studies on shopping district revitalization and public space activation are reviewed to understand post‑disaster social and spatial recovery.
Instructor: 信岡　尚道[NOBUOKA, Hisamichi](能登里山里海未来創造センター)

Subject Name: 復興地域づくり論[Community-Based Post-Disaster Reconstruction]
Theme: Evaluation of Reconstruction (Sustainability and National Resilience)
Details: The effectiveness and limitations of reconstruction plans are evaluated using the lens of sustainability, SDGs, national resilience, and pre‑disaster recovery planning. Using the Noto Peninsula earthquake as a case, students engage in an exercise to propose reconstruction strategies.
Instructor: 信岡　尚道[NOBUOKA, Hisamichi](能登里山里海未来創造センター)

Subject Name: 復興地域づくり論[Community-Based Post-Disaster Reconstruction]

Theme: Structure and function of the nervous system
Details: This section provides an overview of the structural organization of the brain and explains functional localization.

Subject Name: 医療カウンセリング概論Ⅰ
Theme: History and research methods of neuropsychology and physiological psychology
Details: This section reviews the history of neuropsychology and physiological psychology along with the development of research methods. The latter part introduces neuroimaging techniques which are currently the mainstream approach.

Subject Name: 医療カウンセリング概論Ⅰ
Details: This section provides an overview of the temporal classification of memory and introduces amnesia. It also addresses issues specific to the elderly.

Subject Name: 医療カウンセリング概論Ⅰ
Details: This section provides an overview of the role of attention in supporting cognitive activities and the executive functions necessary for goal-directed behavior, and then introduces case examples.

Subject Name: 医療カウンセリング概論Ⅰ
Details: This section provides an overview of the fundamental language functions (comprehension, reading, speech, and writing) and introduces cases where each function is impaired.

Subject Name: 医療カウンセリング概論Ⅰ
Details: This section explains apraxia, a loss of ability to perform intentional movements or actions. It also explains agnosia, a loss of the connection between specific perceptions and their meanings.

Subject Name: 医療カウンセリング概論Ⅰ
Theme: Social behavior disorders, affective disorders, and neurodevelopmental disorder
Details: This section provides an overview of the control of emotions and motivation necessary for social life and introduces case examples. Furthermore, it addresses neurodevelopmental disorders, also known as developmental disabilities.
